name: Safavid Empire

areaKm2.note: Infobox 2.9 million km2 for 1630 (high; Seshat 2.7M for 1501-1722, https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/374). In 1600 Tabriz, Shirvan and Georgia were still Ottoman (1590 treaty) and Kandahar Mughal; the world_1600 polygon measures ~1.61 million km2 (low).

population.note: Infobox 8-10 million for 1650 (Blake 2013); Seshat codes 9 million (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/374); OWID/HYDE Iran 1600 = 5.0M plus western Afghanistan (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). Lower in 1600 with Azerbaijan under Ottoman rule.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Isfahan up to ~200,000 (Seshat largest settlement), Qazvin, Tabriz (Ottoman in 1600), Mashhad, Shiraz.

activePersonnel.note: Abbas's crown-paid army: 10,000-15,000 ghulam cavalry, 12,000 musketeers, 12,000 artillerymen and a 3,000 bodyguard, ~37,000-40,000 in all (Roemer 1986 p. 265, Savory 1980, via the article), plus ~12,000 qurchis/Shahsevans (Blow via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safavid_Iran). In 1600 the reforms (Allahverdi Khan from 1600) were still in progress, hence low 30,000.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Qizilbash tribal cavalry raised by the provincial amirs from tuyul land grants, plus Kurdish, Lur and Georgian contingents.

supportPersonnel.note: Tupchi artillery corps: 12,000 at full strength (Roemer via the article); smaller in 1600, low/mid educated.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Tribal cavalry society plus the new crown army.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 10,000-15,000 ghulam cavalry (Caucasian slave soldiers) and the 3,000 bodyguard (Roemer, Savory via the article), plus part of the ~12,000 qurchis (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safavid_Iran).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: mail, lance, bow and some muskets.

count.note: Tufangchi musketeer corps, 12,000 at full strength (Roemer 1986 p. 265 via the article); still forming in 1600.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: recruited from Iranian peasants, drilled with English help (Shirley brothers).

count.note: Abbas increased his cannon so that he could field 500 in a single battle (Nahavandi and Bomati 1998 via the article) (high, later in the reign); mid for 1600.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: Abbas I and Allahverdi Khan retook Herat (1598) and would take Tabriz (1603) and Yerevan (1604).

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: ghulams loyal to the shah; Qizilbash factionalism (civil wars of the 1580s) only recently curbed.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: recovery after the losses of 1578-90.

weapons.note: Anchor 5 (1600): matchlocks and cannon alongside composite bows.

armor.note: Anchor 4-5: mail and plate-and-mail (chahar aina), helmets.

ships.note: Anchor 2-3: no navy; Caspian and Gulf boats only; Hormuz was taken in 1622 with English ships.

fortification.note: Anchor 4: mudbrick and stone citadels, no bastioned trace.

logistics.note: Anchor 4-5: caravanserai network and Abbas's road building.

gdpPerCapita.note: No Maddison value for Iran before 1820 (877). Analogues: Turkey 1500 = 768, 1650 = 832 (Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). Silk exports lift Iran slightly.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Crown army paid from khassa (crown) lands converted from Qizilbash provinces; low = peacetime.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Silk, carpets, textiles, metalwork.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Qanat-irrigated oases and Caspian rice.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Caravan routes with caravanserais; Abbas's paved causeway in Mazandaran.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. No Gulf port in Safavid hands in 1600 (Hormuz Portuguese, Gombroon taken 1614); Caspian landings only.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Caspian craft; Gulf trade in Portuguese hands.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cavalry armies foraging across the plateau; scorched-earth defence against the Ottomans.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: high arid plateau, long Ottoman supply lines and Safavid scorched-earth defence (Tahmasp vs Suleiman).

notes: Snapshot = 1600, Shah Abbas I in the middle of his military reforms, capital newly moved to Isfahan (1598), Herat retaken, Tabriz still Ottoman. Personnel convention: the crown-paid ghulam, musketeer and artillery corps and the qurchi guard are activePersonnel; Qizilbash tribal cavalry raised by provincial amirs are trainedReserves. Corps sizes are end-of-reign establishment figures (Roemer, Savory, Blow via the Abbas the Great and Safavid Iran articles); Matthee and Floor (Safavid Government Institutions) not consulted directly. Population convention: lands under Safavid rule in 1600 (without Ottoman-held Azerbaijan, Shirvan and Georgia).
